sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtodakaṃ tu rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ puraskṛtya mahābāhur uttatārākulendriyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Putting King Dhṛtarāṣṭra before him, once the water-offerings had been made, the mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, his senses confounded with grief, climbed up from the river.

sanskrit: uttīrya ca mahīpālo bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ papāta tīre gaṅgāyā vyādhaviddha iva dvipaḥ
english: And having ascended, the lord of the earth, his eyes brimming with tears, fell upon the bank of the Gaṅgā like an elephant struck down by a hunter.

sanskrit: taṃ sīdamānaṃ jagrāha bhīmaḥ kṛṣṇena coditaḥ maivam ity abravīc cainaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ parabalārdanaḥ
english: As he sank down, Bhīma, urged on by Kṛṣṇa, took hold of him; and Kṛṣṇa, crusher of hostile armies, said to him, "Do not act so."

sanskrit: tam ārtaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau niśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Anguished, fallen to the ground, sighing again and again, O king, the Pāṇḍavas beheld the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā dīnamanasaṃ gatasattvaṃ janeśvaram bhūyaḥ śokasamāviṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samupāviśan
english: Seeing the lord of men downcast in heart and drained of his strength, the Pāṇḍavas, overcome anew with sorrow, sat down beside him.

sanskrit: rājā ca dhṛtarāṣṭras tam upāsīno mahābhujaḥ vākyam āha mahāprājño mahāśokaprapīḍitam
english: And King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the mighty-armed, the deeply wise, seated near him, spoke these words to the one tormented by overwhelming grief.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha kuruśārdūla kuru kāryam anantaram kṣatradharmeṇa kauravya jiteyam avanis tvayā
english: "Rise, O tiger among the Kurus, and do the task that comes next. By the law of the warrior, O Kauravya, this earth has been won by you.

sanskrit: tāṃ bhuṅkṣva bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ suhṛdbhiś ca janeśvara na śocitavyaṃ paśyāmi tvayā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Enjoy it together with your brothers and your friends, O lord of men. I see nothing here for you to mourn, O best of those who uphold the law.

sanskrit: śocitavyaṃ mayā caiva gāndhāryā ca viśāṃ pate putrair vihīno rājyena svapnalabdhadhano yathā
english: It is I who must mourn, and Gāndhārī too, O lord of peoples, bereft of our sons and our kingdom, like one whose wealth was won only in a dream.

sanskrit: aśrutvā hitakāmasya vidurasya mahātmanaḥ vākyāni sumahārthāni paritapyāmi durmatiḥ
english: Having failed to heed the words of deepest meaning spoken by the great-souled Vidura, who sought my good, I, fool that I am, now burn with regret.

sanskrit: uktavān eṣa māṃ pūrvaṃ dharmātmā divyadarśanaḥ duryodhanāparādhena kulaṃ te vinaśiṣyati
english: Long ago that righteous-souled one of divine sight told me: 'Through Duryodhana's transgression your whole line will perish.'

sanskrit: svasti ced icchase rājan kulasyātmana eva ca vadhyatām eṣa duṣṭātmā mando rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: 'If you wish well-being, O king, for your line and for yourself, let this evil-natured, dull-witted prince Suyodhana be put to death.

sanskrit: karṇaś ca śakuniś caiva mainaṃ paśyatu karhi cit dyūtasaṃpātam apy eṣām apramatto nivāraya
english: Let neither Karṇa nor Śakuni so much as set eyes on him ever again; vigilant, forbid even their gathering for the dicing.'

sanskrit: abhiṣecaya rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram sa pālayiṣyati vaśī dharmeṇa pṛthivīm imām
english: 'Consecrate as king the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira; self-controlled, he will guard this earth in accordance with the law.'

sanskrit: atha necchasi rājānaṃ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram meḍhībhūtaḥ svayaṃ rājyaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva pārthiva
english: 'But if you will not have Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira for king, then become the very pivot yourself and take up the kingdom, O prince.'

sanskrit: samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu vartamānaṃ narādhipa anujīvantu sarve tvāṃ jñātayo jñātivardhana
english: 'Bearing yourself with even regard toward all beings, O ruler of men, let all your kinsmen live under your protection, O increaser of your kin.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kaunteya vidure dīrghadarśini duryodhanam ahaṃ pāpam anvavartaṃ vṛthāmatiḥ
english: Though far-seeing Vidura spoke thus, O son of Kuntī, I, with my mind turned to vanity, followed the wicked Duryodhana.

sanskrit: aśrutvā hy asya vīrasya vākyāni madhurāṇy aham phalaṃ prāpya mahad duḥkhaṃ nimagnaḥ śokasāgare
english: For not having listened to that hero's gentle words, I have reaped a great misery as their fruit, and am sunk in an ocean of sorrow.

sanskrit: vṛddhau hi te svaḥ pitarau paśyāvāṃ duḥkhitau nṛpa na śocitavyaṃ bhavatā paśyāmīha janādhipa
english: For your two parents here are aged, O king, and you see us both stricken with grief; yet I see nothing for which you should mourn, O lord of men."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu rājñā sa dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dhīmatā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva medhāvī tam uvācātha keśavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the wise King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the sagacious one fell silent; and then Keśava spoke to him.

sanskrit: atīva manasā śokaḥ kriyamāṇo janādhipa saṃtāpayati vaitasya pūrvapretān pitāmahān
english: "Grief nursed too greatly in the heart, O lord of men, scorches even the ancestors long departed before him.

sanskrit: yajasva vividhair yajñair bahubhiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ devāṃs tarpaya somena svadhayā ca pitṝn api
english: Offer sacrifice with many and varied rites, with ample priestly fees; gratify the gods with soma, and the fathers too with the ancestral oblation.

sanskrit: tvadvidhasya mahābuddhe naitad adyopapadyate viditaṃ veditavyaṃ te kartavyam api te kṛtam
english: For one such as you, O great of intellect, this present grief is not fitting; what is to be known you have known, and what was to be done you have done.

sanskrit: śrutāś ca rājadharmās te bhīṣmād bhāgīrathīsutāt kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāc caiva nāradād vidurāt tathā
english: You have heard the duties of kings from Bhīṣma, the son of the Bhāgīrathī, and likewise from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, from Nārada, and from Vidura.

sanskrit: nemām arhasi mūḍhānāṃ vṛttiṃ tvam anuvartitum pitṛpaitāmahīṃ vṛttim āsthāya dhuram udvaha
english: You should not follow this course that befits the deluded; take up rather the way of your fathers and forefathers, and bear the yoke of rule.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ hi yaśasā kṣatraṃ svargaṃ prāptum asaṃśayam na hi kaś cana śūrāṇāṃ nihato 'tra parāṅmukhaḥ
english: For the warrior, joined with glory, attains heaven beyond doubt; and not one among the brave was slain here with his back turned.

sanskrit: tyaja śokaṃ mahārāja bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā na śakyās te punar draṣṭuṃ tvayā hy asmin raṇe hatāḥ
english: Cast off your sorrow, O great king, for what was to be has come to pass thus; those slain by you in this battle can never be seen again.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā govindo dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram virarāma mahātejās tam uvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having said this much to the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, the mighty-splendored Govinda fell silent; and Yudhiṣṭhira answered him.

sanskrit: govinda mayi yā prītis tava sā viditā mama sauhṛdena tathā premṇā sadā mām anukampase
english: "Govinda, the love you bear me is well known to me; with friendship and affection you have ever shown me your tender care.

sanskrit: priyaṃ tu me syāt sumahat kṛtaṃ cakragadādhara śrīman prītena manasā sarvaṃ yāvadanandana
english: And it would be the greatest of kindnesses to me, O wielder of the discus and the mace, O glorious giver of every joy, if with a willing heart you did all this.

sanskrit: yadi mām anujānīyād bhavān gantuṃ tapovanam na hi śāntiṃ prapaśyāmi ghātayitvā pitāmaham karṇaṃ ca puruṣavyāghraṃ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinam
english: If only you would grant me leave to go to the forest of penance; for I see no peace, having caused the death of our grandfather, and of Karṇa, that tiger among men who never fled from battle.

sanskrit: karmaṇā yena mucyeyam asmāt krūrād ariṃdama karmaṇas tad vidhatsveha yena śudhyati me manaḥ
english: By what deed I might be freed from this cruel act, O tamer of foes—ordain that deed for me here, by which my mind may be made clean."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ vyāsas tataḥ provāca dharmavit sāntvayan sumahātejāḥ śubhaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: To him who spoke thus, Vyāsa, knower of the law, of vast splendor, then spoke—comforting him with auspicious words full of meaning:

sanskrit: akṛtā te matis tāta punar bālyena muhyase kim ākāśe vayaṃ sarve pralapāma muhur muhuḥ
english: "Your understanding is unformed, my child; through childishness you are bewildered once again. Are we all to keep babbling into the empty air, over and over?

sanskrit: viditāḥ kṣatradharmās te yeṣāṃ yuddhena jīvikā yathā pravṛtto nṛpatir nādhibandhena yujyate
english: Known to you are the duties of the warrior, whose livelihood is in war; a king who has acted as ordained is not bound by the fetters of guilt.

sanskrit: mokṣadharmāś ca nikhilā yāthātathyena te śrutāḥ asakṛc caiva saṃdehāś chinnās te kāmajā mayā
english: And the entire doctrine of liberation you have heard truly as it is; more than once I myself have severed your doubts that spring from desire.

sanskrit: aśraddadhāno durmedhā luptasmṛtir asi dhruvam maivaṃ bhava na te yuktam idam ajñānam īdṛśam
english: Faithless, dull of wit, your memory clearly gone astray—do not be so; such ignorance as this is not worthy of you.

sanskrit: prāyaścittāni sarvāṇi viditāni ca te 'nagha yuddhadharmāś ca te sarve dānadharmāś ca te śrutāḥ
english: All the rites of expiation are known to you, O sinless one; all the laws of war and all the laws of giving you have heard.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ sarvadharmajñaḥ sarvāgamaviśāradaḥ parimuhyasi bhūyas tvam ajñānād iva bhārata
english: How is it that you, knower of all laws, master of all the sacred lore, are bewildered yet again as though from ignorance, O Bhārata?"

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yudhiṣṭhira tava prajñā na samyag iti me matiḥ na hi kaś cit svayaṃ martyaḥ svavaśaḥ kurute kriyāḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Yudhiṣṭhira, your discernment is not sound—such is my judgment. For no mortal of his own accord, master of himself, performs his deeds.

sanskrit: īśvareṇa niyukto 'yaṃ sādhv asādhu ca mānavaḥ karoti puruṣaḥ karma tatra kā paridevanā
english: Appointed by the Lord, this man does the good and the evil; the person performs the deed—what cause for lamentation is there in that?

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ manyase cātha pāpakarmāṇam antataḥ śṛṇu tatra yathā pāpam apakṛṣyeta bhārata
english: And if in the end you deem yourself a doer of evil, then hear how the evil may be drawn away from you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tapobhiḥ kratubhiś caiva dānena ca yudhiṣṭhira taranti nityaṃ puruṣā ye sma pāpāni kurvate
english: By austerities, by sacrifices, and by giving, O Yudhiṣṭhira, those men who have done evil deeds forever cross beyond them.

sanskrit: yajñena tapasā caiva dānena ca narādhipa pūyante rājaśārdūla narā duṣkṛtakarmiṇaḥ
english: By sacrifice, by penance, and by giving, O ruler of men, O tiger among kings, are men who have done ill deeds made pure.

sanskrit: asurāś ca surāś caiva puṇyahetor makhakriyām prayatante mahātmānas tasmād yajñāḥ parāyaṇam
english: Both the Asuras and the gods, those great-souled ones, strive to perform the rite of sacrifice for the sake of merit; therefore sacrifices are the surest refuge.

sanskrit: yajñair eva mahātmāno babhūvur adhikāḥ surāḥ tato devāḥ kriyāvanto dānavān abhyadharṣayan
english: It was through sacrifices that the great-souled gods became supreme; and then the gods, rich in rites, overpowered the Dānavas.

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedhau ca sarvamedhaṃ ca bhārata naramedhaṃ ca nṛpate tvam āhara yudhiṣṭhira
english: The Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha, the Sarvamedha, O Bhārata, and the Naramedha too—offer them, O king, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yajasva vājimedhena vidhivad dakṣiṇāvatā bahukāmānnavittena rāmo dāśarathir yathā
english: Sacrifice with the horse-sacrifice, duly performed and richly endowed with priestly fees, with abundance of choice food and treasure, as Rāma the son of Daśaratha did.

sanskrit: yathā ca bharato rājā dauḥṣantiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ śākuntalo mahāvīryas tava pūrvapitāmahaḥ
english: And as did King Bharata, son of Duḥṣanta, lord of the earth, the son of Śakuntalā, of mighty valor, your own ancient forefather.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asaṃśayaṃ vājimedhaḥ pāvayet pṛthivīm api abhiprāyas tu me kaś cit taṃ tvaṃ śrotum ihārhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Beyond doubt the horse-sacrifice would purify even the whole earth; yet I have a certain thought, which you ought to hear here.

sanskrit: imaṃ jñātivadhaṃ kṛtvā sumahāntaṃ dvijottama dānam alpaṃ na śakyāmi dātuṃ vittaṃ ca nāsti me
english: Having wrought this vast slaughter of my kinsmen, O best of the twice-born, I cannot bring myself to give even a small gift—and treasure I have none.

sanskrit: na ca bālān imān dīnān utsahe vasu yācitum tathaivārdravraṇān kṛcchre vartamānān nṛpātmajān
english: Nor can I bring myself to beg wealth of these wretched children, these sons of kings still bleeding from fresh wounds and dwelling in distress.

sanskrit: svayaṃ vināśya pṛthivīṃ yajñārthe dvijasattama karam āhārayiṣyāmi kathaṃ śokaparāyaṇān
english: Having myself laid the earth waste, O most excellent of the twice-born, how shall I levy tribute for the sake of sacrifice from those given over to grief?

sanskrit: duryodhanāparādhena vasudhā vasudhādhipāḥ pranaṣṭā yojayitvāsmān akīrtyā munisattama
english: Through Duryodhana's transgression the earth and the lords of the earth have perished, fastening upon us an enduring infamy, O best of sages.

sanskrit: duryodhanena pṛthivī kṣayitā vittakāraṇāt kośaś cāpi viśīrṇo 'sau dhārtarāṣṭrasya durmateḥ
english: By Duryodhana the earth was wasted for the sake of wealth, and that treasury of the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is itself emptied away.

sanskrit: pṛthivī dakṣiṇā cātra vidhiḥ prathamakalpikaḥ vidvadbhiḥ paridṛṣṭo 'yaṃ śiṣṭo vidhiviparyayaḥ
english: And in this rite the earth itself is the sacrificial fee—such is the ordinance of the first and highest order, beheld by the learned; any departure from it is a lesser prescription.

sanskrit: na ca pratinidhiṃ kartuṃ cikīrṣāmi tapodhana atra me bhagavan samyak sācivyaṃ kartum arhasi
english: And I have no wish to make any substitute for it, O you whose wealth is penance; in this, O blessed one, you ought to render me your full counsel.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu pārthena kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā muhūrtam anusaṃcintya dharmarājānam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the son of Pṛthā, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana then, having pondered a moment, spoke to the Dharma-king.

sanskrit: vidyate draviṇaṃ pārtha girau himavati sthitam utsṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇair yajñe maruttasya mahīpateḥ tad ānayasva kaunteya paryāptaṃ tad bhaviṣyati
english: "There is treasure, O Pārtha, lying in the Himavat mountain, left behind by the brāhmaṇas at the sacrifice of King Marutta. Bring that, O son of Kuntī; it will be sufficient."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ yajñe maruttasya draviṇaṃ tat samācitam kasmiṃś ca kāle sa nṛpo babhūva vadatāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was that treasure heaped up at the sacrifice of Marutta, and in what age did that king come to be, O best of speakers?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yadi śuśrūṣase pārtha śṛṇu kāraṃdhamaṃ nṛpam yasmin kāle mahāvīryaḥ sa rājāsīn mahādhanaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: If you wish to hear, O Pārtha, listen concerning King Karaṃdhama, and in what age that mighty and greatly wealthy king lived.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śuśrūṣe tasya dharmajña rājarṣeḥ parikīrtanam dvaipāyana maruttasya kathāṃ prabrūhi me 'nagha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I long to hear, O knower of the law, the full recital of that royal seer; O Dvaipāyana, tell me the tale of Marutta, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca āsīt kṛtayuge pūrvaṃ manur daṇḍadharaḥ prabhuḥ tasya putro maheṣvāsaḥ prajātir iti viśrutaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: In the Kṛta age of old there was Manu, the lord who bore the rod of rule; his son was a great archer renowned by the name Prajāti.

sanskrit: prajāter abhavat putraḥ kṣupa ity abhiviśrutaḥ kṣupasya putras tv ikṣvākur mahīpālo 'bhavat prabhuḥ
english: Prajāti's son was the one widely known as Kṣupa; and Kṣupa's son was Ikṣvāku, who became a guardian of the earth and a sovereign lord.

sanskrit: tasya putraśataṃ rājann āsīt paramadhārmikam tāṃs tu sarvān mahīpālān ikṣvākur akarot prabhuḥ
english: He had a hundred sons, O king, supremely righteous; and Ikṣvāku the lord made every one of them a guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhas tu viṃśo 'bhūt pratimānaṃ dhanuṣmatām viṃśasya putraḥ kalyāṇo viviṃśo nāma bhārata
english: The eldest of them was Viṃśa, a paragon among bowmen; and Viṃśa's noble son was named Viviṃśa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: viviṃśasya sutā rājan babhūvur daśa pañca ca sarve dhanuṣi vikrāntā brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: Viviṃśa had sons, O king, fifteen in number, all valiant with the bow, devoted to the brāhmaṇas, and speakers of the truth.

sanskrit: dānadharmaratāḥ santaḥ satataṃ priyavādinaḥ teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ khanīnetraḥ sa tān sarvān apīḍayat
english: Given to the law of giving, virtuous, and ever sweet of speech; the eldest among them was Khanīnetra, and he oppressed them all.

sanskrit: khanīnetras tu vikrānto jitvā rājyam akaṇṭakam nāśaknod rakṣituṃ rājyaṃ nānvarajyanta taṃ prajāḥ
english: But Khanīnetra, valiant though he was, having won the kingdom free of thorns, could not keep it; the people did not give him their love.

sanskrit: tam apāsya ca tad rāṣṭraṃ tasya putraṃ suvarcasam abhyaṣiñcata rājendra muditaṃ cābhavat tadā
english: And casting him aside, that realm consecrated his son Suvarcas, O lord of kings, and then there was rejoicing.

sanskrit: sa pitur vikriyāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyān nirasanaṃ tathā niyato vartayām āsa prajāhitacikīrṣayā
english: Beholding his father's misdeed and his expulsion from the kingdom, he, self-restrained, conducted himself in the wish to do good to the people.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ satyavādī ca śuciḥ śamadamānvitaḥ prajās taṃ cānvarajyanta dharmanityaṃ manasvinam
english: Devoted to the brāhmaṇas, truthful, pure, endowed with calm and self-mastery—and the people gave their love to that high-minded one, ever steadfast in the law.

sanskrit: tasya dharmapravṛttasya vyaśīryat kośavāhanam taṃ kṣīṇakośaṃ sāmantāḥ samantāt paryapīḍayan
english: As he held to the path of righteousness, his treasury and his forces wasted away; and the neighboring kings, his treasury now drained, beset him on every side.

sanskrit: sa pīḍyamāno bahubhiḥ kṣīṇakośas tv avāhanaḥ ārtim ārchat parāṃ rājā saha bhṛtyaiḥ pureṇa ca
english: Hard-pressed by the many, his treasury spent and his forces gone, the king fell into the deepest distress, together with his servants and his city.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ parihartuṃ te 'śaknuvan parisaṃkṣaye samyagvṛtto hi rājā sa dharmanityo yudhiṣṭhira
english: Yet in his utter ruin they could not bring themselves to forsake him, for that king was right in his conduct and ever steadfast in the law, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yadā tu paramām ārtiṃ gato 'sau sapuro nṛpaḥ tataḥ pradadhmau sa karaṃ prādurāsīt tato balam
english: But when that king with his city had come to the utmost distress, then he blew upon his hand, and from it an army sprang into being.

sanskrit: tatas tān ajayat sarvān prātisīmān narādhipān etasmāt kāraṇād rājan viśrutaḥ sa karaṃdhamaḥ
english: Then he conquered all those bordering kings; and for this reason, O king, he became renowned as Karaṃdhama.

sanskrit: tasya kāraṃdhamaḥ putras tretāyugamukhe 'bhavat indrād anavaraḥ śrīmān devair api sudurjayaḥ
english: His son Kāraṃdhama was born at the dawn of the Tretā age, no less than Indra, glorious, and hard for even the gods to conquer.

sanskrit: tasya sarve mahīpālā vartante sma vaśe tadā sa hi samrāḍ abhūt teṣāṃ vṛttena ca balena ca
english: In his sway all the guardians of the earth then abided; for he became their sovereign emperor, by his conduct and by his might.

sanskrit: avikṣin nāma dharmātmā śauryeṇendrasamo 'bhavat yajñaśīlaḥ karmaratir dhṛtimān saṃyatendriyaḥ
english: His name was Avikṣit, righteous of soul, the equal of Indra in valor; devoted to sacrifice, delighting in rites, steadfast, and master of his senses.
